clue.text: Down and dirty

blocks.note: feeling down is feeling low in spirits
a dirty joke or film is a risqué, smutty one

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'down and dirty' pretends to be one idiom; split it and each half is a separate sense of the same colour word.
explanation.definitionFit: Two meanings of one colour word: gloomy and sad in mood, or smutty and risqué as with a racy comedy routine.

clue.text: Small settlement, a tragedy

blocks.note: a tiny village, smaller than a town
Shakespeare's play about the Prince of Denmark

explanation.surface: A little village that has suffered some disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma makes it look as though the settlement suffered a tragedy; in fact the village and the play simply share a name.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny rural village is called this, and Shakespeare's famous Danish revenge play carries exactly the same title.

clue.text: Select the best fruit before harvest

indicators.note: in a down clue 'before' puts the fruit word above the harvest word

blocks.note: a small red stone fruit
to harvest fruit is to pick it

explanation.surface: Advice to a fruit grower: sort out the finest produce before the crop comes in.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is so orchard-bound that the pieces barely feel disguised; the trick is that the whole phrase also names the answer's figurative meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: To choose only the most favourable items from a range, like picking only the ripest cherries off a tree.

clue.text: Look at animals on top of slope

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sitting 'on' another is placed above it
the top of a down-written word is its first letter, so take the start of 'slope'

blocks.note: donkeys, plural
first letter of slope

explanation.surface: Someone surveys livestock grazing up at the top of a hillside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On top of slope' reads as a place in the scene, but it is two instructions: 'on' places the animals above, and 'top of' keeps one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To evaluate or weigh something up, examining it carefully in order to form a judgement about its quality or value.

clue.text: Balloon, something round and white

blocks.note: as a verb, to balloon is to grow rapidly and uncontrollably
a packed sphere of winter flakes, thrown in fun

explanation.surface: Describing a balloon: a round white thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Balloon' looks like a noun that the rest describes; it is really a verb, a separate definition from the round white object.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to grow faster and faster; as a noun it is a hand-packed sphere of snow.

clue.text: Island in Cuba, lively

indicators.note: 'in' tells us the island sits inside the words that follow

blocks.note: spans the end of Cuba and the start of lively

explanation.surface: A lively island somewhere in Cuba.
explanation.walkthrough: Cuba is itself an island, so the reader goes looking for a Caribbean islet; the answer is on the other side of the world, straddling two words.
explanation.definitionFit: An Indonesian island and popular holiday destination east of Java, famous for its temples and surfing beaches.

clue.text: The Albion playing after missing European event

indicators.note: the team is 'missing' a player before it plays, so one letter is dropped first
the players move around the pitch, so the letters of the team name change places

blocks.note: anagram fodder, nine letters
E is the standard abbreviation for European; it is removed

explanation.surface: A football team called the Albion takes the field short of its European player.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove one E from the team name, then rearrange the remaining eight letters. Albion is a nickname for English clubs such as West Bromwich Albion.
explanation.definitionFit: A sporting competition combining two disciplines, usually cross-country skiing with rifle shooting at the Winter Olympics.

clue.text: Morphing is for green aliens

indicators.note: morphing is changing shape, so the following letters change their order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, ten letters

explanation.surface: Shape-shifting is a trick favoured by little green men from outer space.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface paints science-fiction green aliens; 'aliens' is really the older legal sense of people from another country.
explanation.definitionFit: In law and older usage, people living in a country where they are not citizens are known by both terms.

clue.text: Strike keeping Everton, initially, in lead

indicators.note: 'initially' asks for just the opening letter of the club's name
to keep something is to hold it, so the strike word holds the club's letter

blocks.note: to lash is to strike with a whip
first letter of Everton

explanation.surface: A footballer goes on strike while Everton sit top of the league.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In lead' looks like part of the football story (Everton leading the table); 'lead' is the definition, a dog's lead. Everton is a Liverpool football club.
explanation.definitionFit: A strap or cord attached to a dog's collar for walking it is called both a lead and this word.

clue.text: Smaller country Romanians abandoned

indicators.note: abandoned means wild and unrestrained, so the letters run wild into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, nine letters

explanation.surface: Romania left a smaller nation behind, or its citizens emigrated from it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abandoned' reads as leaving somewhere; here it means unrestrained, the anagram signal. The definition is fair because it is a tiny country, far smaller than Romania.
explanation.definitionFit: A microstate enclaved within Italy, one of the world's tiniest independent republics, far smaller than Romania.

clue.text: 5 Down general’s thrown about

indicators.note: something thrown about lands in disorder, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, seven letters

explanation.surface: A general gets pelted with snowballs.
explanation.walkthrough: 5 Down is SNOWBALL, so the surface pictures an officer being pelted; here the cross-reference is used in its verb sense, to balloon or grow.
explanation.definitionFit: To grow or make bigger, just as a problem that snowballs keeps swelling in size and scale.

clue.text: Sound from ref, ending in shrill note at end of game

indicators.note: 'ending in shrill' points only to the final letter of that word
the letter and the note are placed at the end of the card game

blocks.note: a card game for four players
final letter of shrill
E is a note of the musical scale

explanation.surface: The referee's shrill blast signals full time.
explanation.walkthrough: The game at the end looks like a football match; it is the card game whist. The whole surface also describes the answer, blown at the final whistle.
explanation.definitionFit: A referee blows this small instrument to stop and start play, making a high piercing noise on the pitch.

clue.text: Where boat may stop like a plane?

blocks.note: a landing stage projecting into the water
read whimsically as jet plus -y, resembling an aircraft; the question mark flags the invented sense

explanation.surface: A question about where a boat can moor, as if it were an aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a playful coinage, like an adjective such as 'leafy', built from a noun for an aircraft; the question mark admits the invention.
explanation.definitionFit: A small pier or landing stage jutting out into water where boats tie up to load passengers.

clue.text: Start before then scoffing odd bits of grub — go early

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters, first and third, of the food word are kept
to scoff is to eat greedily, so 'then' swallows the kept letters
'start' comes before the rest in the answer

blocks.note: to start is to jump in surprise
taken literally
letters one and three of grub

explanation.surface: Someone starts eating before everyone else and grabs bits of food: a bad table manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Then' is used as itself. The definition is fair because a runner who jumps the gun leaves before the starting pistol.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom from athletics: to act prematurely, setting off before the starting pistol has actually been fired.

clue.text: Start and stop part of engine

indicators.note: 'and' simply joins the two verbs end to end

blocks.note: to spark something is to start it off
to plug a hole is to stop it up

explanation.surface: Stop-start: a piece of a car engine that switches it on and off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start and stop' reads like a feature of a car engine; the two verbs are separate pieces, and 'stop' means block, not halt.
explanation.definitionFit: The component in a petrol engine that ignites the fuel mixture in each cylinder with an electric discharge.

clue.text: Case in quitting sport

indicators.note: the case word goes 'in' the quitting word, splitting it

blocks.note: kicking a habit is quitting it
a box is a case or container

explanation.surface: A legal case about someone giving up a sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' looks like a lawsuit and 'quitting' like retirement; one is a container and the other is kicking, as in kicking a habit.
explanation.definitionFit: A combat discipline in which fighters strike each other with both fists and feet in a ring.

clue.text: Union pass?

blocks.note: surface reading: a pass for a trade union, or a pass in rugby union
setter's reading: the official permit that allows a wedding to go ahead

explanation.walkthrough: Two words invite a trade union card or rugby union; the union is a wedding and the pass is the legal permit to hold it.
explanation.definitionFit: The official document authorising a couple to wed, a permit for the union of two people in matrimony.

clue.text: Check out toasted nuts, eating last of four

indicators.note: 'last of four' takes only the final letter of that number word
nuts means crazy, so the letters of 'toasted' go crazy into a new order
the shuffled word eats the extra letter, taking it into the fodder

blocks.note: anagram fodder, seven letters
final letter of four

explanation.surface: Someone samples roasted nuts, eating the last four.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toasted nuts' looks like a snack; 'nuts' is the anagram signal, and 'last of four' is one letter, not the final four nuts.
explanation.definitionFit: To try out a vehicle, or any product, in real conditions before buying or approving it for use.

clue.text: Bird: that thing below moving target

indicators.note: a moving target shifts about, so its letters shift into a new order
in a down clue 'that thing' sits below the rearranged target

blocks.note: anagram fodder, six letters
it is the pronoun for a thing

explanation.surface: A bird flying beneath a moving target, as at a shooting range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving target' reads as a fixed phrase, but 'moving' is the anagram signal. This is a common garden bird in Britain, with a black head and yellow breast.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest European member of the titmouse family, a common black, white and yellow garden songbird.

clue.text: Talks she organised around opening of negotiations, unrewarded

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, so take the start of 'negotiations'
to organise is to put into order, so the letters get sorted into a new one
the rearranged letters go around the extra letter, taking it into the fodder

blocks.note: anagram fodder, eight letters
first letter of negotiations

explanation.surface: She set up talks and opened negotiations but got no credit for it.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a diplomat's unappreciated work, which is also the answer's meaning; 'talks she' is the letters to shuffle, not a conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes a task or job that brings no gratitude or appreciation from those who benefit from it.

clue.text: Understand about wave, something nasty in the water?

indicators.note: the understand word goes about, around, the wave word

blocks.note: 'I see' means I understand
to wag a finger or tail is to wave it

explanation.surface: Grasping that there is something unpleasant lurking in the sea around a wave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wave' pulls toward the sea; it is a verb here, to wag. The question mark admits the definition is a description rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Waste matter and effluent carried off in drains, unpleasant stuff sometimes discharged into rivers and the sea.

clue.text: Bread sauce

blocks.note: slang for money, as bread is
sauce is cheek or impudence, nerve

explanation.walkthrough: Bread sauce is a British accompaniment to roast chicken, so the pair reads as one dish; each word is a separate slang definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British slang for money, and also for cheeky nerve or impudence, as in having the brass neck.

clue.text: Fuss over ruby, very dear

indicators.note: in a down clue 'over' places the fuss word above the ruby word

blocks.note: as in much ado about nothing
ruby is a shade of red

explanation.surface: Someone making a fuss over an expensive ruby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very dear' looks like the price of the jewel; it is the definition, meaning much loved.
explanation.definitionFit: Loved deeply and held in great affection, the way a cherished person is precious to someone.

clue.text: Beseech delicacy of headless chicken?

indicators.note: the bird word loses its head, the first letter

blocks.note: hen without its first letter
a delicacy is a treat

explanation.surface: A plea for a titbit from a chicken running around with its head cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chicken' here is a hen; with its head gone it leaves two letters that come before the delicacy.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to ask someone earnestly or anxiously for something, as a humble plea or appeal.

clue.text: Top grade ultimately raised in test

indicators.note: 'grade ultimately' is the final letter of that word
in a down clue, raising the letters makes them read from bottom to top

blocks.note: max is the top, the maximum
final letter of grade

explanation.surface: A top grade achieved at last in a test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top grade' reads as an A; 'top' is the maximum and 'grade' gives only its last letter, and the pair is flipped upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal assessment of a student's knowledge, sat in a hall and marked for grades.

clue.text: Figure that’s still in job after increase

indicators.note: the job word comes after the increase word

blocks.note: to wax is to grow, as the moon waxes
a job is work

explanation.surface: Someone who is still in their job after getting a pay rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure' reads as a person or number and 'still' as yet; together they are the definition, a model that never moves, as at Madame Tussauds in London.
explanation.definitionFit: A life-size model of a person sculpted from wax and displayed in a museum, standing motionless.

clue.text: Hold keys, entering every pantry, first of all

indicators.note: 'first of all' takes the first letter of each of the words before it

blocks.note: initial letters of the four words

explanation.surface: Keep hold of the keys when you go into each larder.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a housekeeper's instruction; the four words in the middle are just a source of initial letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To retain possession of something or keep hold of it, not letting it go or giving it away.

clue.text: Awful puns in rag, without mercy

indicators.note: something awful is in a bad state, so the letters are in a bad order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, nine letters

explanation.surface: A merciless verdict on the terrible wordplay in a tabloid newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: A rag is slang for a low-quality newspaper, and 'in' is part of the fodder, not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Harsh, severe, and showing no leniency or pity towards anyone, giving no quarter at all.

clue.text: Relative peace finally in part of France

indicators.note: 'peace finally' keeps only the last letter of that word
the letter goes inside the name of the French city

blocks.note: a city on the French Riviera
final letter of peace

explanation.surface: A family member finds peace at last in a region of France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of France' suggests a region; it is the Riviera city Nice, into which a single letter is slipped.
explanation.definitionFit: The daughter of one's brother or sister, a family member one generation down.
